scope: New path-based filesystem writes from an MCP stdio process started with explicit ORGANON_ROOT on supported Linux

negative_control.setup: A real MCP stdio client first invokes init, put, run and status within the explicit root; a separate same-UID test process then moves the pinned case directory outside the root before another put.
negative_control.observed: The relocated put returns an MCP error and the outside ledger bytes remain identical to the pre-move snapshot.

missing_capability_control.observed: A simulated ENOSYS during Landlock setup ends server startup with nonzero status before a request or case mutation.

checks.result: 1629 passed in 242.17s; no expected failures remain

checks.command: uv run ruff check .; git diff --check
uv build --wheel --offline; offline install and uv pip check in fresh Python 3.11.15 and 3.12.3 environments; installed MCP workflow probe
checks.result: Wheel and both installed probes passed with explicit ORGANON_ROOT

independent_review: A read-only reviewer found no concrete regression in the new policy and reproduced the focused tests. The evidence supports only the case-relocation rejection tested here.
limits: Without explicit ORGANON_ROOT, historical development mode retains descriptor pinning but does not install this Landlock write policy.
The policy does not revoke writable file descriptors opened before restriction.
A peer with the same UID remains unrestricted and can alter root topology; moving the root itself is not proven safe.
In-root hardlinks and concurrent hardlink changes remain a separate path and content integrity limit.
This does not authenticate case evidence, approvals, external anchors or real-world impact.
